segments.heading: From a question to a dashboard
lines: Two English sentences become governed SQL,
and the results become a live Superset dashboard.

segments.caption: The Catalyst workbench, pointed at an OpenELIS laboratory database.
No SQL is written by hand — the question is the input.
A writer model drafts the SQL; a reviewer checks it against the approved catalog.
The draft is SQL you can read and edit — then it runs against the real database.
The result is saved as a governed Dataset, with its query and provenance.
Standing guidance is pinned to the session — every later turn must honor it.

segments.heading: Refine in conversation
lines: The follow-up edits the exact query that just ran.

segments.caption: "Now count all results by test name instead…"
The models revise the current query rather than starting over.
The aggregate runs and is saved as a second Dataset.

segments.heading: Build the widgets
lines: A table and a grouped bar, each bound to a saved Dataset.

segments.caption: Widget types are constrained by what the Dataset's columns support.

segments.heading: Publish the dashboard
lines: Catalyst writes a native Superset bundle, deterministically.

segments.caption: Both widgets on one dashboard — published as a Superset bundle.
A pinned importer brings the bundle into Superset and records a receipt.
Imported — Catalyst links straight to the live dashboard.
The finished product: a table and a graph, from one conversation.

segments.heading: A conversation became a dashboard
lines: Small open models drafted and reviewed every query.
Nothing ran that the catalog did not allow.
